summary:
Martian Map is an interactive, multi-layered mission operations and survival guide built to help the first human explorers safely navigate and study Mars.

Astronauts on the Martian surface face extreme terrain hazards, dynamic weather, and severe communication delays with Earth. To survive and succeed, they need immediate, localized access to decades of disconnected planetary data rather than relying solely on mission control.

Our platform solves this by unifying complex datasets into one intuitive spatial interface. It helps astronauts plan safe traverse routes around steep slopes and hazards, monitor real-time solar and environmental conditions, and pinpoint high-value geological targets to conduct meaningful science during time-sensitive Marswalks.

We developed Martian Map as a lightweight, browser-based web application utilizing HTML5 Canvas and JavaScript for real-time 3D orbital and surface rendering. We integrated open-source data layers from multiple NASA missions—combining Viking MDIM 2.1 color mosaics and MOLA elevation models with NASA JPL positional tracking and SDO solar telemetry—to transform raw scientific archives into an actionable field tool.
details:
We built Martian Map, an interactive mission operations dashboard and survival guide designed for the first astronauts walking on Mars. Instead of forcing explorers to dig through separate scientific archives while dealing with a 20-minute communication delay to Earth, our web app pulls decades of NASA data into one live, unified map. You start in a 3D orbital view—complete with Mars’s axial tilt and its moons, Phobos and Deimos—and smoothly zoom down to the surface to inspect terrain, check waypoints, and read localized survival and science notes.

The biggest benefit is turning raw, complicated planetary data into fast, life-saving decisions. On a real Marswalk, every minute of oxygen and battery power counts. Our tool helps astronauts spot dangerous slopes before they walk into them, monitor solar activity, and immediately locate high-priority geological targets so they can do real science without wasting time. We hope this project shows how human-centered interface design can bridge the gap between deep-space telemetry and the actual people working on the ground.

To keep it fast and accessible on any device, we built the entire platform as a lightweight web app using HTML5, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript, relying heavily on HTML5 Canvas for real-time 3D rendering and interactive mapping. We hosted it on GitHub Pages and integrated open-source datasets directly from NASA Trek (Viking MDIM 2.1 color mosaics and MOLA laser altimeter elevation data), NASA JPL for orbital positioning, and NASA SDO for solar monitoring.

What makes our project creative is treating a scientific map like an active field survival guide rather than a static textbook. When designing it, our team constantly put ourselves in the boots of a Marswalker—thinking about cognitive load under stress, how to make complex elevation and radiation data readable at a glance, and how to balance strict safety routing with the freedom to explore new scientific discoveries. Thank you.
